messages:
customer_xyz: Hey team — our production rerank calls started failing ~10m ago. Endpoint /v1/rerank returns 400 for model 'ranker-legacy-v1'. This was working yesterday. Example request attached and response. Can you help?

morgan_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the exact request body and response you see? Also which SDK/version are you using?

customer_xyz: Here you go:
```json
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "model": "ranker-legacy-v1",
  "queries": ["how to reset password"],
  "candidates": [["reset password steps", "forgot password flow"]]
}
```
Response:
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Invalid model identifier: ranker-legacy-v1"
  }
}
```
Using our internal wrapper around the HTTP API, nothing changed on our side.

morgan_support: Thanks — tagging @julia_engineer to check model routing. Can you also send the request id header (x-request-id) from your client if present?

customer_xyz: x-request-id: cc7f9a2b-4e8a-11ee-8c99-0242ac120003

julia_engineer: Looking at control plane logs for that request id — it hit the router but model id resolved to an alias that was removed during a cleanup job last night. The control plane returned a validation error before hitting runtime: "invalid_model: model id not found". I can see a deploy-bot message about deprecating `ranker-legacy-v1` and pointing customers to `ranker-v2` at 2024-11-18T03:12Z.

deploy-bot: Notice: model alias `ranker-legacy-v1` marked deprecated and removed from public catalog (deploy 2024-11-18T03:12Z). Customers should migrate to `ranker-v2` or use tenant-specific pinned model ids.

lee_sre: Quick note — we did a prune of stale public aliases as part of housekeeping. For most customers a redirect alias was in place for a week; looks like this tenant had a cached alias that expired and the redirect entry was accidentally deleted in the same job.

morgan_support: Sorry about the churn. Two parts to fix: 1) get customer back online quickly, 2) prevent silent alias removals. Julia, can we re-create a temporary alias for this tenant so their calls succeed while they migrate?

julia_engineer: Yes. I can re-create a tenant-scoped alias `tenant-123-ranker-legacy` pointing to `ranker-v2` and add a 7-day TTL. That will make their current client succeed immediately. Migration steps: switch to `ranker-v2` and validate scores/regression.

customer_xyz: Appreciate that. Any quick workaround if we can't change model id immediately?

julia_engineer: Two options:
1) If you can add the header `X-Model-Alias: ranker-v2` we can accept that as override for now (short-term fix).
2) Otherwise we'll provision the tenant alias as Morgan suggested. Option 1 is fastest if your client library supports custom headers.

customer_xyz: We'll try header override and report back.

morgan_support: Also note why you saw 400 instead of 410/404 — the control plane's validation path returns 400 for unknown public model ids to avoid leaking tenant mapping info. We do return 410 for explicitly deprecated tenant-pinned IDs; we'll update docs to clarify.

customer_xyz: Header override worked, calls succeeded. Thanks! We still see some score differences vs old model, is that expected?

julia_engineer: Yes, `ranker-v2` has an updated scoring head and tokenization. We recommend running a small eval set (10–50 queries) to check regression. If you need us to run a quick diff, send a sample CSV and we can run an internal eval.

lee_sre: Follow-up actions: 1) create tenant alias `tenant-123-ranker-legacy` (7d TTL) — DONE, 2) schedule rollback guard to keep redirects for 72h during prune jobs — P0 ticket created, 3) doc update for model deprecation error codes — assigned.

morgan_support: Marking thread as resolved for now — please re-open if you see the 400 after the alias TTL expires. :thumbsup:

customer_xyz: Thanks all — will run eval and coordinate migration. :pray:
